name: ringline
workload: Two-machine TCP echo benchmark (9 server configs x 4 message sizes x 4 connection counts, bare-metal Xeon, X710 40G LAG) plus a Segcache GET cache-server workload (256B/1KiB/4KiB values, 128 connections) on AWS Graviton4 c8g instances
claimed_speedup: TCP echo: ~0-10% faster than the best-tuned tokio configuration (tokio-pc/tokio-uring), but 27-71% faster than tokio's default multi-thread runtime depending on size/connections (author flags the larger number as previously overclaimed/misleading). Segcache: +30-31% throughput, -24 to -28% p50 latency, -15 to -18% p99 latency, +22-23% ops/core-s vs tokio at 256B/1KiB values; 4KiB ties on throughput/median latency with +14% CPU efficiency and -8% p99
compiler_and_flags: Rust stable; exact rustc version and build flags not stated
hardware: Echo run: bare-metal 24 vCPU Xeon server / 56 vCPU Xeon client, 4x Intel X710 in 40G LAG (exact CPU model number not given). Segcache run: AWS Graviton4 (Neoverse-V2) c8g.4xlarge server / c8g.8xlarge client, aarch64
tradeoffs: Only ~0-10% faster than tokio's best-tuned configurations; the larger 27-71% figure holds only against tokio's default (non-per-core) config. Loses to a zero-copy tokio+splice path at 16KiB payloads. Requires manual worker-count tuning matched to concurrency for best CPU efficiency. Linux-focused (io_uring/epoll/mio backends).
caveats: First-party benchmark published in the project's own repo, not independent; capped below Tier A because exact CPU model (echo run just says 'Xeon') and exact compiler flags/rustc version are not stated, despite otherwise rigorous methodology (Little's law validity gates, stated rig, reproduction steps). Segcache numbers are from June 2026 on an older release (0.1.3) and have not been re-run on current ringline. The project's own README explicitly retracts an earlier version of this file that quoted the 27-71% figure while implying it beat tokio's best configuration rather than only its default.
found_via: GitHub search 'io_uring event loop' sorted by recently updated (gh search repos), surfaced ringline-rs/ringline; cross-checked against crates.io io_uring listings
